title: Sigmoidoscopy
description: Sigmoidoscopy is a procedure where your doctor uses a flexible camera to examine your sigmoid colon (lower part of your large intestine) and rectum. This procedure helps diagnose problems like inflammation, tumors, polyps, bleeding sources, or infections in your lower colon. Your doctor will perform a bowel preparation with an enema or laxative to clear your colon for better visualization. During the procedure, you'll be awake and may feel mild pressure or cramping as the camera advances. You can usually return to normal activities immediately after sigmoidoscopy, without needing sedation or a driver. If your doctor finds concerning areas, they may take biopsies or recommend additional testing. Sigmoidoscopy examines only your lower colon, unlike colonoscopy which examines your entire large intestine.
